review_cost.rationale: One round of changes before approving: adopt generated route types, unify 404 handling, evict failed cache promises, add a fetch timeout. All are local edits; no architectural rework is needed.

findings.issue: getJSON caches rejected promises for the process lifetime and suppresses them with promise.catch(() => {}); speciesIndexPromise (line 95) does the same. A single transient API failure permanently breaks the home page and any affected resource until restart.
findings.suggestion: On rejection, delete the cache entry (cache.delete(url) in a catch) and reset the index promises to null on failure; consider AbortSignal.timeout on fetch.

findings.issue: All route components take loaderData: any and all loaders hand-declare args, ignoring the generated ./+types route types that React Router v8 (and the project's own `react-router typegen` script) provide.
findings.suggestion: Import Route from ./+types/<route> and use Route.LoaderArgs / Route.ComponentProps so loader data is end-to-end typed.

findings.issue: 404 handling is a { notFound: true } loader flag branched on in the component, duplicated across four routes, while the root ErrorBoundary independently renders the same NotFound UI for thrown errors — two mechanisms for one concern.
findings.suggestion: Follow the documented pattern: throw data("Not Found", { status: 404 }) from loaders and render a shared ErrorBoundary/NotFound, or a single shared throwNotFound helper.

findings.issue: The root ErrorBoundary renders the 'Not found' UI for every error, including 500s and dev errors, hiding real failures.
findings.suggestion: Inspect the thrown error (isRouteErrorResponse) and show a distinct error message for non-404s.

findings.issue: The home loader ignores the request URL; all 1,025 species plus per-generation id lists are serialized into every response and filtered client-side, diverging from the loader-driven search-params pattern the framework recommends.
findings.suggestion: Either parse q/type/generation in the loader (even partially, e.g. server-side slice the current page), or keep the client-side design but document the tradeoff and trim the payload (generation id lists are redundant with a small species→generation map).

findings.issue: Document titles are set by rendering <title> inside components instead of the framework's meta export (works only via React 19 hoisting).
findings.suggestion: Move titles to a meta export on each route module.

findings.issue: hiddenBySpecies encodes a Map as an object that the component (line 43) decodes back into a Map, duplicating the hidden flag already present on each pokemon entry.
findings.suggestion: Pass the hidden flag through with the entries and drop the hiddenBySpecies map.

findings.issue: searchParamsRef.current = searchParams mutates a ref during render, which React guidance discourages and can misbehave under concurrent rendering.
findings.suggestion: Assign the ref inside a useEffect, or read searchParams from props at event time via a stable closure.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache Map is unbounded with no eviction; fine against this fixed API snapshot but a silent foot-gun if the data source grows.
findings.suggestion: Cap size (LRU) or at least document the assumption that the API's key space bounds the cache.

summary: A tidy, readable framework-mode app that loads data the right way (server loaders, cached over HTTP, clean .server boundary) and gets the fiddly accessibility and URL-state requirements right. The main gaps are ignoring the generated route types the framework (and the project's own typegen script) provide, a duplicated ad-hoc 404 pattern alongside a misleading root ErrorBoundary, and a promise cache that permanently stores failures. One round of targeted fixes would make it an easy approve.
